subject: humanities
passage: Mexican painter Frida Kahlo returned to the same subject again and again: more than fifty of her paintings are self-portraits. Some viewers have dismissed this focus as narrow, the work of an artist who looked no further than the mirror. Yet Kahlo used her own face and body to explore subjects far larger than herself, including Mexican national identity, physical suffering, and the place of women in society. Her self-portraits, then, are far less ______ than they might first appear.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: "Yet" signals that the author disagrees with viewers who called Kahlo's focus "narrow." Because the paintings explore "subjects far larger than herself," they are less narrow than they seem. "Limited" expresses that idea.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The author shows that the paintings take on large subjects, so they are more ambitious than they appear, not less.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text defends Kahlo's work; nothing suggests that her paintings are less skillful than they seem.
explanation.C: Correct. The author argues that the self-portraits reach well beyond Kahlo herself, so they are less limited than the "narrow" label suggests.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how bright or striking the paintings look; it is about the range of their subjects.
